description: The plot illustrates the training loss over iterations for several large language model variants, including a baseline “Vanilla” model and multiple configurations of the proposed SepLLM and StrmLLM methods, with different segment sizes (n=64 or n=128) and optional hierarchical or hybrid training (H, H/T). The x-axis, labeled “#Iteration,” spans from 0 to 140,000 in linear scale with major gridlines and tick labels every 20,000 iterations. The y-axis, labeled “Loss,” ranges from 2.4 to 3.4 in linear scale, with major tick marks and gridlines every 0.1 unit. The “Vanilla” model (purple line) starts near 3.4 and decreases steadily to approximately 2.5 by 140,000 iterations. The “StrmLLM (n=64)” (blue line) begins slightly below 3.4, drops rapidly to ~2.7 by 20,000 iterations, then gradually declines to ~2.62. “SepLLM (n=64)” (orange line) follows a similar trajectory, starting near 3.4, falling to ~2.7 by 20,000, and ending at ~2.58. “SepLLM (n=64, H)” (green line) begins near 3.4, drops to ~2.7 by 20,000, and stabilizes around 2.55. “SepLLM (n=64, H/T)” (red line) starts near 3.4, falls to ~2.7 by 20,000, and ends near 2.53. “SepLLM (n=128)” (dark blue line) starts near 3.4, drops to ~2.75 by 20,000, and ends near 2.6, showing a slightly higher final loss compared to the n=64 variants. All lines exhibit a steep initial decline followed by a slower, more gradual decrease, indicating convergence.
